newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains, seen up on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains, seen up on Wednesday.

text.p: Polish shares extended Monday's slight gains to 15,269.8 points and analysts saw another rise on Wednesday as the market rebounded from recent falls linked with flooding and an interest-rate rise.
On Monday Poland's lombard rate went up by two points to 27 percent and the discount rate by 2.5 points to 24.5 percent while overall damage from July's floods is seen in the billions of dollars.
"It seems as if bad information has been discounted, for example the flooding,...and 15,000 of WIG provides support," said Roman Skorka, trader at Polish Investment Bank brokerage.
Analysts said the market's upside was limited during the run-up to Poland's parliamentary elections due on September 21.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.8 percent to 15,269.8 points and turnover rose 17.7 percent to 149.8 million zlotys ($43 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 46 to 38 with 23 stocks flat.
Bank Slaski rose 9.9 percent after falling the same amount on Monday, a drop analysts said likely represented speculation after the interest-rate announcement.
They said industrial boilermaker Rafako, suspended from bourse trade since July 11, should fall on Wednesday when it returns without the daily 10-percent price-fluctuation limit.
On Monday the firm gave an 18.9-million-zloty ($5.4 million) preliminary flood damage estimate but said this year's sales forecast of 370 million zlotys ($106.2 million) had not been changed.

Analysts said paintmaker Polifarb Wroclaw, up five percent, was doing well after announcing last week that 11.6-million- zloty ($3.3 million) flood damage had forced it to lower its 1997 net profit forecast by only 10.2 percent.
